# Disagreement Log — 2 Maccabees Chapter 12
**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 22

---

## V.3 — "impious act" vs. "impiety" vs. "particularly vicious act"
- EMET: "impious act"
- LOGOS: "impiety"
- PNEUMA: "particularly vicious act" (loses the religious/cultic sense)
- SOPHIA: "impiety" — Greek *asebēma*: impious act/sacrilege; LOGOS preferred

## V.4 — "common vote of the city" vs. "general decision of the city" vs. "official city decision"
- EMET: "common vote"
- LOGOS: "general decision"
- PNEUMA: "official city decision"
- SOPHIA: LOGOS — Greek *koinē gnōmē*: common/general opinion or resolution

## V.6 — "called on God, the just judge" — all agree on epithet
- Minor variation: EMET uses comma placement differently; no substantive disagreement
- All render "just judge" for *dikaios kritēs*

## V.13 — "certain city that was strongly fortified with walls" vs. "strongly fortified with ramparts and walls" vs. "fortified city"
- LOGOS adds "ramparts" — Greek *periblema kai teichesin*: embankment/ramparts and walls
- PNEUMA simplifies to "fortified city" (loses the specific defenses)
- SOPHIA: LOGOS phrasing retained — the two separate defenses matter contextually

## V.14 — "things that were not lawful to say" vs. "things that were not lawful to utter" vs. "things that were too wicked to repeat"
- EMET: "not lawful to say"
- LOGOS: "not lawful to utter"
- PNEUMA: "too wicked to repeat" (loses the legal/cultic register)
- SOPHIA: LOGOS phrasing

## V.16 — "unspeakable slaughters" vs. "a slaughter beyond all telling" vs. "slaughter beyond description"
- EMET: "unspeakable slaughters" (plural, archaic)
- LOGOS: "a slaughter beyond all telling" (elegant)
- PNEUMA: "slaughter beyond description"
- SOPHIA: LOGOS phrasing

## V.22 — "manifestation of him who sees all things" — all three agree
- PNEUMA paraphrases: "they knew what it meant when God — who sees everything — showed his hand" — interpretive expansion
- SOPHIA: retain literal "manifestation of him who sees all things"

## V.24 — "with great cunning" vs. "with great cunning" vs. "Timothy was clever"
- EMET/LOGOS: "with great cunning"
- PNEUMA: transforms into narrator comment ("Timothy was clever")
- SOPHIA: EMET/LOGOS — the adverbial phrase belongs to Timothy's action, not a narrator aside

## V.40 — "sacred tokens of the idols" vs. "sacred tokens of the idols" vs. "amulets sacred to the idols"
- EMET/LOGOS: "sacred tokens" (Greek *hiera*: sacred things/tokens)
- PNEUMA: "amulets" (an interpretive identification — amulets are likely correct but not explicit)
- SOPHIA: "sacred tokens" — retain the Greek *hiera*; "amulets" is possible but interpretive

## V.43 — "sin offering" — all three agree
- Greek *peri hamartias* = sin offering; all render correctly
- Critical note: Any rendering other than "sin offering" would be theologically erroneous here

## V.43 — "with an eye toward the resurrection of the dead" vs. "with the resurrection of the dead in view" vs. "in full view of the resurrection of the dead"
- EMET: "with an eye toward the resurrection of the dead"
- LOGOS: "with the resurrection of the dead in view"
- PNEUMA: "done in full view of the resurrection of the dead"
- SOPHIA: "with the resurrection of the dead in view" — LOGOS; most natural English

## V.44 — "superfluous and foolish" vs. "superfluous and foolish" vs. "pointless and absurd"
- EMET/LOGOS: "superfluous and foolish"
- PNEUMA: "pointless and absurd"
- SOPHIA: "superfluous and foolish" — Greek *perisson kai lēron*: superfluous and trifling/foolish; retain specific terms

## V.45 — "fall asleep in godliness" vs. "fall asleep in godliness" vs. "die in faithfulness to God"
- EMET/LOGOS: "fall asleep in godliness" — retain death-as-sleep metaphor
- PNEUMA: "die in faithfulness to God" (loses the sleep metaphor)
- SOPHIA: "fall asleep in godliness" — *kekoimēmenois meta eusebeias*: the sleep metaphor is deliberate and theologically significant

## V.45 — "holy and pious" vs. "holy and devout" vs. "holy and right"
- EMET: "holy and pious"
- LOGOS: "holy and devout"
- PNEUMA: "holy and right" (loses *eusebes* = pious/devout)
- SOPHIA: "holy and devout" — LOGOS; *hosios kai eusebes*

## V.45 — "made atonement for the dead" — all three agree
- Greek *hilasmon epoiēsato peri tōn teteleutēkotōn*: made atonement/propitiation for the dead
- Critical: all three correctly render "made atonement" — must not be softened

## V.45 — "delivered from their sin" vs. "released from their sin" vs. "set free from their sin"
- EMET: "delivered"
- LOGOS: "released"
- PNEUMA: "set free"
- SOPHIA: "released" — Greek *apolythōsin*: loosed/released; LOGOS preferred

## STRUCTURAL — V.9 distance notation
- EMET: "two hundred and forty stadia"
- PNEUMA: "240 stadia" (numeral)
- SOPHIA: spell out numbers in running prose

## STRUCTURAL — V.20 army numbers
- PNEUMA uses numerals (120,000; 2,500); EMET/LOGOS spell out
- SOPHIA: LOGOS convention — spell out for consistency with rest of translation

## V.26 — "slaughtered twenty-five thousand persons" vs. "slaughtered twenty-five thousand persons" vs. "killed twenty-five thousand people"
- PNEUMA: "killed" (acceptable but weaker)
- SOPHIA: "slaughtered" — matches the violence of the original *katekopsan*

## V.31 — "feast of Weeks" vs. "feast of Weeks" vs. "feast of Weeks"
- All three agree; minor: LOGOS has "feast of Weeks" in v. 31 and "Pentecost" in v. 32 — same event, matching the Greek text's double reference
- PNEUMA has "feast of Weeks" / "festival of Pentecost" — consistent

## V.35 — Dositheus arm severing — all three agree on the details
- Minor variation: EMET "cut off his arm at the shoulder" / LOGOS "cut off his arm at the shoulder" / PNEUMA "slashed off his arm at the shoulder"
- SOPHIA: EMET/LOGOS phrasing

## V.37 — "raised a battle cry in the Hebrew tongue" vs. "raising the battle cry in the Hebrew language" vs. "with a battle cry in Hebrew"
- EMET: "in the Hebrew tongue"
- LOGOS: "in the Hebrew language"
- PNEUMA: "in Hebrew"
- SOPHIA: "in the Hebrew language" — LOGOS
